faqs.q: What does Hazard Perception Mock Test 1 cover?
faqs.a: Mock Test 1 focuses on beginner hazard perception skills, including spotting developing hazards, reacting to pedestrians, noticing junction risks and learning when a situation may require you to slow down.

faqs.q: Is this an official DVSA hazard perception test?
faqs.a: No. This is independent hazard perception practice designed to help learners revise and build confidence. It is not an official DVSA test.

faqs.q: How should I use this mock?
faqs.a: Use this mock to practise spotting hazards early, then review your result and focus on the situations you missed before moving to the next mock.

commonMistakes: Focusing only on the vehicle directly ahead
Missing hazards caused by parked cars
Reacting late to cyclists or pedestrians
Forgetting to watch junctions and side roads
2.whoFor: Candidates who want a short check on parked vehicle hazards in Hazard Perception revision.

faqs.q: What does Hazard Perception Mock Test 2 help me practise?
faqs.a: Mock Test 2 helps you practise spotting hazards linked to parked vehicles, cyclists, pedestrians, side roads and changing traffic conditions.

faqs.q: Can I retake this hazard perception mock?
faqs.a: Yes. Retaking the mock can help you notice patterns in the hazards you miss and improve your timing and observation.

faqs.q: What should I focus on during this mock?
faqs.a: Focus on the whole road scene, not just the vehicle in front. Watch pavements, junctions, parked cars and vulnerable road users.

faqs.q: What does Hazard Perception Mock Test 3 cover?
faqs.a: Mock Test 3 focuses on developing traffic hazards, visibility clues, road layout changes and timing your response when a risk begins to develop.

faqs.q: Why is timing important in hazard perception?
faqs.a: Timing matters because the aim is to recognise a developing hazard early enough, not after the danger has already become obvious.

faqs.q: What should I do once you complete this mock?
faqs.a: Review the hazards you missed, then practise again while focusing on earlier observation, traffic movement and clues from the road environment.

faqs.q: What does Mock Test 4 focus on?
faqs.a: Mock Test 4 is centred on parked-car hazards and pedestrians near the kerb. It helps you practise looking into gaps between vehicles, side roads and pavements where a risk may start to develop.

faqs.q: Who should try Mock Test 4?
faqs.a: Learners who need more confidence with urban observation should use this mock, especially if they often miss hazards near parked vehicles or side streets.

faqs.q: What should I review after Mock Test 4?
faqs.a: Review whether you noticed pedestrians and vehicle movement around parked cars early enough. Pay attention to side roads, doorways and gaps between vehicles where hazards can appear suddenly.

faqs.q: What road users appear in Mock Test 5?
faqs.a: Mock Test 5 concentrates on cyclists, motorcyclists and pedestrians. The key skill is spotting when a vulnerable road user may change position, slow down or move into the driver's path.

faqs.q: Who should use Mock Test 5?
faqs.a: This mock is useful if you want to improve your awareness of smaller or more exposed road users who may be harder to see in traffic.

faqs.q: How can I improve after Mock Test 5?
faqs.a: Focus on road users who are smaller or harder to see, such as cyclists and motorcyclists. Rewatch similar practice clips and look for signs that they may change lane, slow down or move into your path.

faqs.q: What should I look for in Mock Test 6?
faqs.a: Look for movement at junctions and side roads before it becomes obvious. Check vehicle position, indicators and gaps where another driver may emerge or turn across your path.
